concept.shortExplanation: Everything from the last four chapters is one block: tokens in, embeddings looked up, positions added, attention mixing information across positions, a residual and a norm, a feed-forward layer transforming each position independently, another residual and norm. Stack that block a few dozen times, project the final state back to vocabulary size, softmax, and you have the architecture behind every model in this course. Assemble it correctly and you will run a real forward pass through a live causal language model, watching each stage produce the input to the next.
concept.ahaMoment: There is no separate reasoning component. Everything the model does is this one block repeated, and capability came from repeating it more times on more text rather than from adding new kinds of machinery.

levels.title: Order the Pipeline
levels.instructions: Drag the stages into the order data actually flows through a transformer block. A wrong order will not run.
hints: Tokens have to exist and be turned into vectors before anything numeric can happen to them — start with tokenize and embed, then work out what has to happen before attention can mix information across positions at all.

Attention needs a query, key and value before it can attend to anything, and its output gets added back to what came in (a residual) and normalised before the feed-forward layer touches it. That add-then-normalise pattern happens a second time after the feed-forward layer, then the block is done.
Verified order: tokenize, embed, positional-encoding, qkv-projection, attention, residual-add-1, layer-norm-1, feed-forward, residual-add-2, layer-norm-2, unembed, softmax.

levels.title: Fill the Gaps
levels.instructions: Some stages have been removed from the block. Restore the missing ones — leaving a stage out changes what the block can compute, and the scoring reflects which omissions actually break it.
hints: Four stages are missing. Two of them are the 'add the input back' steps that appear right after attention and right after the feed-forward layer — the residual connections.

positional-encoding has to land between embed and qkv-projection, or every position looks identical to attention. softmax is marked critical here — it's what turns raw scores into next-token probabilities — so leaving it out costs double what a merely-missing layer-norm does.

Verified: the missing stages are positional-encoding (right after embed), residual-add-1 (right after attention), layer-norm-2 (right after the second residual add) and softmax (the very last stage, after unembed).

levels.title: Run It End to End
levels.instructions: Your assembled pipeline now drives a real forward pass through GPT-2 on your own prompt. Every stage renders its true intermediate output. Predict the model's top token from the stage outputs alone, before the final softmax is revealed.

hints: The given prompt's real top-5 is genuinely close together, not a case with one obvious answer — read the actual percentages once they're shown rather than guessing from intuition. All three rounds count toward the score and an unanswered round scores as wrong, so add and answer all of them before submitting.

Verified against the real model for "The first rule of debugging is to": the renormalised top-5 is make 23.1%, use 20.4%, find 20.4%, be 18.0%, not 18.0% — the real top token is 'make', with 'use' and 'find' tied close behind at this model's precision.

For your own rounds, a confident prompt is easier to call than the default one: "I think therefore I" verifies to am 30.1%, should 20.7%, 'm 19.4%, have 17.2%, can 12.6% — a clear, wide leader, unlike the default prompt's close race.
